The test image shows a mango leaf with dark brown/black irregular spots scattered across the leaf surface. The spots are discrete, roughly circular to irregular in shape, and distributed across the leaf blade. The leaf is otherwise greenish.

Key features: dark necrotic spots, irregular/angular lesions, no white powdery coating, no sooty black coating covering large areas, no tip/branch dieback.

This pattern of discrete dark spots is characteristic of **Anthracnose** (caused by *Colletotrichum* spp.), not Powdery Mildew (white powder), Sooty Mould (uniform black coating), or Die Back (tip necrosis).

Let me confirm with one reference image from Anthracnose.

The reference Anthracnose image shows more advanced browning/necrosis. The test image shows an earlier stage with discrete dark spots on a green leaf, which is still most consistent with Anthracnose. The other classes don't fit: no white powder (Powdery Mildew), no uniform sooty black coating (Sooty Mould), no tip necrosis/dieback (Die Back).
